newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa rebound may be capped at 1,067 stg.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa rebound may be capped at 1,067 stg.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Cocoa futures are likely to rebound further after Thursday's steep losses, but the second-month September contract may struggle to clear 1,067 stg a tonne on the upside, analysts said on Monday.
Traders said the market was due unchanged to a couple of stg lower.
The New York futures market was closed on Friday for the U.S. Independence Day holiday.
After hitting a double top at around 2,700 stg in late May, September futures slid through two weeks of consolidation to touch the multiple lows at 1,000 stg established since April.
Trevor Neil, a senior technical analyst at Cal Futures Ltd, said the market started a small upward reaction on Friday.
It hit an intraday high of 1,040 stg on Friday.
Neil said the market might successfully test a minor resistance at 1,044 but it could fail at the next levels of 1,067 and the bottom of a chart gap at 1,087. The top of the gap was 1,103.
On the downside, a break of 1,000 would be negative and would indicate a test of the lows at 900 stg, he said.
Fundamentally, the second quarter U.K. and Dutch cocoa grind data released on Friday were within market expectation.
The German data were due on Monday. "The key figure will be the German grind, which, because of a major reorganisation of capacity, few are confident in giving predictions," broker GNI said.
It said the market was still technically in recovery mode after the sharp losses last week, "but prices will only rise if the trade start to do some serious bargain hunting."
